hello.note: Reply: wacalaykum salaam. Used by Somalis everywhere, at any time of day.

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: aad baad u mahadsan tahay. To several people: mahadsanidiin.

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'you deserve it'. Also: waxba ma aha (it's nothing).

excuse_me.note: To catch someone's eye Somalis often just call walaal (brother/sister); an older man: adeer.

im_fine.note: Short everyday answer: waa nabad (all is peace).

nice_to_meet_you.text: Waan ku faraxsanahay inaan ku barto

where_from.note: Asking about the country: dalkee baad ka timid?

dont_understand.note: Past tense, as Somalis say it. 'I didn't understand you': kuma fahmin.

speak_slowly.text: Fadlan si tartiib ah u hadal

what.note: Also maxaa?, e.g. maxaa dhacay? (what happened?)

why.note: In a sentence use maxaa … u: maxaad u timid? (why did you come?)

who.note: e.g. yaa yimid? (who came?). 'Who is it?': waa kuma?

how_much.note: In the south you will also hear meeqa: kani waa meeqa?

where_bathroom.text: Fadlan, musqushu xaggee bay ku taal?

one.note: Before a noun use hal: hal koob (one cup).

tea.note: Tea with milk: shaah caano leh.

bread.note: The Somali breakfast flatbread is canjeero (laxoox in the north).

menu_please.note: Small eateries often have no menu; ask: maxaad haysaan? (what do you have?)

bill_please.note: Or ask: immisa baad iga leedahay? (how much do I owe you?)

enjoy_meal.note: Hosts usually invite you to start eating with bismillaah (in God's name).

straight_ahead.note: Literally 'go straight'; the word on its own is toos.

stop_here.note: Literally 'drop me here'. Also: halkan ku joogso (stop here).

airport.note: In Mogadishu people often say madaarka.

hotel.note: In Somalia hoteel often means a restaurant too; ask for a qol (room) if you want to sleep.

want_to_go.note: To a taxi driver: … i geey (take me to …).

id_like_this.note: Kan is for masculine nouns; for a feminine one say tan.

pay_card.note: In Somalia most people pay by mobile money (phone transfer) rather than card.

later.note: Also: goor dambe (at a later time).

good_evening.note: Fiid is the evening, from sunset. In the afternoon say galab wanaagsan.

good_night.note: Before bed also: nabad ku seexo (sleep in peace).

see_you_later.note: To several people: hadhow ayaan idin arki doonaa.

help.note: Shouted to everyone around; to one person: i caawi!

call_police.note: To several people: booliiska u yeera!

dont_feel_well.note: If you are ill: waan xanuunsanahay (I'm sick).

maybe.note: Also: waxaa laga yaabaa (it may be that …).

dont_know.note: Also very common: ma ogi, garan maayo.

my_family.note: In everyday speech also reerkayga (my household).

father.note: My father: aabbahay. Also spelled aabe.

brother.note: One word for brother and sister; masculine here: walaalka (the brother), walaalkay (my brother).

sister.note: Same word as brother, but feminine: walaasha (the sister), walaashay (my sister).

child.note: Children: carruur. Son: wiil; daughter: gabadh (gabar in the south).

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: tani waa saaxiibadday.

are_you_married.note: Literally 'have you married?'; the same for a man or a woman.

monday.note: 'On Monday': Isniinta, e.g. Isniinta ayaan imanayaa (I'm coming on Monday).

tuesday.note: Like all Somali day names it comes from Arabic: literally 'the third (day)'.

wednesday.note: The c is a throaty sound, the Arabic ʿayn, squeezed deep in the throat.

thursday.note: Kh is a rough sound, like ch in Scottish 'loch'.

friday.note: The weekly day off and day of prayer. 'On Friday': Jimcaha.

saturday.note: The Somali working week starts on Saturday.

sunday.note: X is a strong breathy h, as in Axmed (Ahmed). A normal working day in Somalia.

weekend.note: Literally 'the end of the week'. In Somalia the weekly day off is Friday (Jimce).

what_day.note: Answer: maanta waa Jimce (today is Friday).

next_week.note: Usbuuc is also common: usbuuca soo socda. Last week: toddobaadkii hore.

eleven.note: Literally 'one and ten': the unit comes first. You will also hear toban iyo kow.

twenty.note: 21 is kow iyo labaatan: the unit comes first.

fifty.note: Irregular, not built from shan (5). Compare afartan (40) and lixdan (60).

how_old.note: In the south you will also hear: meeqa jir baad tahay?

years_old.note: e.g. waxaan ahay soddon jir (I'm thirty). Jir means '-year-old'.

red.note: After a noun: shaati cas (a red shirt). The colour as a noun: casaan.

blue.note: After a noun add ah: shaati buluug ah (a blue shirt).

green.note: After a noun add ah: shaati cagaar ah (a green shirt).

yellow.note: After a noun add ah: shaati jaalle ah. Also: huruud.

black.note: After a noun: shaati madow (a black shirt).

white.note: Careful: cad is white, cas is red. The colour as a noun: caddaan.

another_one.note: Bring me another one: mid kale ii keen.

its_hot.note: Very hot: kulayl badan baa jira.

its_cold.note: Feeling cold yourself: qabow baa i haya.

its_raining.note: The ' is a glottal stop, a short catch in the voice: da-'aya.

its_sunny.note: Literally 'there is sun'. When it comes out after clouds: qorraxdu way soo baxday.

weather_today.note: Hawo means both 'air' and 'weather'; cimilo is also used.

beautiful_day.note: Also: maanta hawadu way fiican tahay (the weather is nice today).

summer.note: Somali seasons follow the rains; xagaa is the dry season after the gu' rains, roughly July to September.

winter.note: The long dry season, roughly December to March: hot in the south, cool in the northern highlands.

room.note: The room: qolka. Room key: furaha qolka.

luggage.note: One bag or suitcase: shandad. Your belongings in general: alaab.

wifi_password.note: Fure (key) is used for a password; many people also just say 'password'.

check_out_time.note: Literally 'when does one leave the room?'.

next_train.note: For a bus: baska xiga goorma buu baxayaa?

is_this_seat_free.note: Literally 'is anyone sitting here?'. Kursi is a seat or chair.

what_do_you_do.note: Also: shaqadaadu waa maxay? (what is your job?)

i_work_in.note: e.g. waxaan ka shaqeeyaa bangi (I work in a bank).

im_student.note: A woman can say the same, or ardayad baan ahay.

meeting.note: I'm in a meeting: shir baan ku jiraa.

day_off.note: Fasax on its own means leave or a holiday.

colleague.note: Literally 'work friend'. A female colleague: saaxiibad shaqo.

good_job.note: Somalis also praise good work with mashaallah!

what_recommend.note: In a small eatery just ask: maxaa ugu fiican? (what's best?)

not_spicy.note: Basbaas is chilli; it is often served as a sauce on the side.

vegetarian_food.note: Make it clear with: hilib ma cuno (I don't eat meat).

no_sugar.note: Somali tea comes very sweet; for just a little say sonkor yar.

im_full.note: Hosts will insist; a polite firm answer: alxamdulillaah, waan dhergay.

takeaway.note: Literally 'wrap it for me'. Also: waan qaadanayaa (I'm taking it with me).

keep_change.note: Baaqi is the change left over.

head_hurts.note: For the stomach: caloosha baa i xanuunaysa.

have_fever.note: Qab is used for illnesses: hargab baan qabaa (I have a cold).

call_ambulance.note: To several people: ambalaas u yeera!

dentist.note: Ilko are teeth; a toothache: ilig xanuun.

lets_meet.note: Literally 'let's see each other'. More formal: aan kulanno.

your_number.note: Also: lambarkaaga i sii (give me your number).

see_you_soon.note: Also: ilaa aan is aragno (until we meet again).

good_luck.note: Before an exam or a task Somalis often say: Allaha kuu fududeeyo (may God make it easy).

thanks_a_lot.note: To several people: aad baad u mahadsan tihiin.

miss_you.note: Past tense, as Somalis say it. To several people: waan idin xiisay.
